# Final Research Questions - LLM-based Unit Test Generation

Date: 2026-06-04  
Source: `SLR/gap-analysis.md`, `experiment/design-rationale.md`

## RQ1 - Primary Research Question

**RQ1:** On the same set of unit-test-generation tasks, do unit tests generated by a structured/chain-of-thought prompt achieve higher mutation score than unit tests generated by a zero-shot prompt?

## RQ2 - Secondary Research Question

**RQ2:** On the same set of unit-test-generation tasks, do unit tests generated by a structured/chain-of-thought prompt achieve higher branch coverage than unit tests generated by a zero-shot prompt?

## PICO Mapping

| Component | RQ1 | RQ2 |
|---|---|---|
| P - Problem / Population | Unit-test-generation tasks or small real-world functions | Unit-test-generation tasks or small real-world functions |
| I - Intervention | Structured/chain-of-thought prompt | Structured/chain-of-thought prompt |
| C - Comparison | Zero-shot prompt | Zero-shot prompt |
| O - Outcome | Mutation score | Branch coverage |

## Scope Notes

- RQ1 is the primary RQ because mutation score is more directly related to fault detection than coverage alone.
- RQ2 is secondary because branch coverage is a common metric in the selected evidence table.
- This RQ set uses a comparative baseline rather than an absolute threshold because the evidence table does not provide enough numerical results to support a threshold value.
